learn.hook: 'Mangoes are the best fruit' starts an argument. '7 is a prime number' ends one. Maths loves sentences that are clearly true or clearly false!
points: A proposition (mathematical statement) is a sentence that is either true or false, but not both.
Questions, commands, exclamations and opinions are not propositions: 'Is 5 odd?', 'Shut the door', 'Maths is fun'.
A sentence like x + 3 = 7 is an open sentence: it becomes true or false only once x is known.
Many propositions have the form 'If P, then Q'. P is the hypothesis and Q is the conclusion.
A statement about ALL cases is false if even one counterexample exists. The negation of 'All birds can fly' is 'Some birds cannot fly' (not 'No birds can fly').

example.q: Is 'Every odd number is prime' a proposition? Is it true?
steps: It makes a clear claim that is either true or false, so it is a proposition
Test: 9 is odd, but 9 = 3 × 3 is not prime
One counterexample is enough, so the statement is false
example.answer: It is a proposition, and it is false (counterexample: 9)

learn.reallife: Courts, contracts and computer programs all rely on statements that must be clearly true or false. 'If the PIN is correct, then open the account' is a proposition in code!

games.title: Proposition or not?
items: 7 is a prime number
The sum of the angles of a triangle is 200°
Every square is a rectangle
Is 15 divisible by 3?
Please solve this sum
Cricket is the most exciting sport
What a lovely rangoli!

games.title: Judge the statement
items: Every square is a rectangle
A square has four right angles and opposite sides equal, so it fits the definition of a rectangle.
Every rectangle is a square
A 4 cm by 2 cm rectangle is a counterexample: its sides are not all equal.
2 is the only even prime number
Every other even number is divisible by 2, so it has at least three factors.
The sum of two odd numbers is odd
3 + 5 = 8, which is even. In fact the sum of two odd numbers is always even.
'2 + 2 = 5' is not a proposition because it is false
False sentences are still propositions. A proposition just has to be true or false.
The square of any real number is never negative
Positive × positive and negative × negative are both positive, and 0² = 0.

quiz.q: Which of these is a proposition?
quiz.explain: '7 is a prime number' is definitely true or false (it is true). The others are a command, a question and an opinion.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any sentence with a number in it is a proposition

quiz.q: Which proposition is false?
options: The angles of a triangle add up to 200°
quiz.explain: The angles of a triangle always add up to 180°, so the statement about 200° is false.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 'every square is a rectangle' is false because squares and rectangles have different names

quiz.q: What is the negation of 'All birds can fly'?
quiz.explain: To deny 'all', you only need at least one exception. Penguins and ostriches show some birds cannot fly.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the opposite of 'all' is 'none'

quiz.q: Which number is a counterexample to 'Every odd number is prime'?
quiz.explain: 9 is odd but not prime, since 9 = 3 × 3. A counterexample must satisfy the 'if' part and break the claim.
quiz.mistake: Picks 2, which is prime but not odd, so it does not test the claim

quiz.q: In 'If a number ends in 0, then it is divisible by 5', what is the hypothesis?
quiz.explain: The hypothesis is the 'if' part: a number ends in 0. The conclusion is the 'then' part.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the hypothesis (if part) with the conclusion (then part)

quiz.q: Is 'x + 3 = 7' a proposition?
options: Not on its own; it becomes true or false only once x is known
No, because it has an equals sign
quiz.explain: It is true when x = 4 and false otherwise, so on its own it is an open sentence.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every equation is automatically a true statement

quiz.q: Which whole number is a counterexample to 'n² > n for every whole number n'?
quiz.explain: 1² = 1, which is not greater than 1. (0 also works.) For 3, 5 and 10 the claim holds.
quiz.mistake: Tests only large numbers, where the claim happens to be true

quiz.q: Riya says 'Every rectangle is a square.' Which reply proves her wrong?
options: A 4 cm × 4 cm square is a rectangle
A 4 cm × 2 cm rectangle is not a square
quiz.explain: One rectangle that is not a square is a counterexample, and that is enough to show the claim is false.
quiz.mistake: Gives an example that agrees with the claim, which cannot disprove it

teach.ask: Gappu chirps: "Is 'Laddoos are yummy' a mathematical statement? It sounds true to me!"
teach.praise: A proposition must be clearly true or false, not both. 'Laddoos are yummy' is an opinion, so it isn't one, even if I agree!
teach.nudge: Can everyone agree whether 'laddoos are yummy' is true or false? What must a proposition always be?

learn.hook: 'If you are in Jaipur, you are in Rajasthan' is true. But 'If you are in Rajasthan, you are in Jaipur'? Swapping can change everything!
points: The converse of 'If P, then Q' is 'If Q, then P': the hypothesis and conclusion swap places.
A true statement can have a false converse. 'If a number is divisible by 4, it is even' is true, but 6 is even and not divisible by 4.
Some statements and their converses are both true, such as Pythagoras' theorem and its converse.
When a statement and its converse are both true, we can join them with 'if and only if'.
To show a converse is false, give one counterexample: a case where Q is true but P is false.

example.q: Write the converse of 'If x = 3, then x² = 9' and decide whether it is true.
steps: Swap the parts: 'If x² = 9, then x = 3'
Test x = −3: (−3)² = 9, but x is not 3
example.answer: Converse: If x² = 9, then x = 3. It is false (x = −3).

learn.reallife: 'If it is a mango, it is a fruit' is true, but 'If it is a fruit, it is a mango' would leave the banana seller very upset!

games.title: Match each statement with its converse
pairs: If it rains, the ground gets wet
If the ground gets wet, it rains
If n is divisible by 6, n is divisible by 3
If n is divisible by 3, n is divisible by 6
If a shape is a square, it has four sides
If a shape has four sides, it is a square
If x = 5, then 2x = 10
If 2x = 10, then x = 5
If I am in Pune, I am in Maharashtra
If I am in Maharashtra, I am in Pune

games.title: Is the converse true?
items: If x = 5, then 2x = 10
If a triangle has three equal sides, it has three equal angles
If a number is a multiple of 10, it ends in 0
If n is divisible by 6, n is divisible by 3
If a shape is a square, it has four sides
If x = 3, then x² = 9
If I am in Pune, I am in Maharashtra

quiz.q: What is the converse of 'If it is raining, then the ground is wet'?
options: If it is not raining, the ground is not wet
If the ground is wet, then it is raining
If the ground is not wet, it is not raining
It is raining and the ground is wet
quiz.explain: The converse swaps the hypothesis and the conclusion.
quiz.mistake: Adds 'not' to both parts instead of swapping them

quiz.q: 'If a number is divisible by 4, then it is even' is true. What about its converse?
options: True, because 8 is even and divisible by 4
False, because 6 is even but not divisible by 4
quiz.explain: The converse is 'If a number is even, it is divisible by 4'. The even number 6 is not divisible by 4, so the converse is false.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one example that works (like 8) proves a statement for all numbers

quiz.q: Which statement has a TRUE converse?
options: If a quadrilateral is a square, it has four right angles
If a triangle has three equal sides, it has three equal angles
If n is divisible by 6, then n is divisible by 3
quiz.explain: A triangle with three equal angles also has three equal sides, so this converse is true. The others fail: x = −3, a rectangle, and n = 9.
quiz.mistake: Assumes that if a statement is true, its converse must be true too

quiz.q: Which value of x shows that 'If x² = 9, then x = 3' is false?
quiz.explain: (−3)² = 9, so the 'if' part holds, but x is not 3.
quiz.mistake: Picks 3, which agrees with the statement instead of breaking it

quiz.q: 'If two angles are vertically opposite, then they are equal' is true. Is its converse true?
options: Yes, equal angles are always vertically opposite
No, two angles can be equal without being vertically opposite
Yes, but only for right angles
quiz.explain: The converse says 'If two angles are equal, they are vertically opposite'. Two 60° angles in an equilateral triangle are equal but not vertically opposite.
quiz.mistake: Assumes every true statement has a true converse

quiz.q: By the converse of Pythagoras' theorem, which triangle is right-angled?
quiz.explain: 7² + 24² = 49 + 576 = 625 = 25². When the squares of the two shorter sides add up to the square of the longest side, the triangle is right-angled.
steps: Equal, so there is a right angle opposite the side 25
quiz.mistake: Adds the sides instead of their squares

quiz.q: 'A triangle is equilateral if and only if all its angles are 60°.' What does 'if and only if' tell us?
options: Both the statement and its converse are true
quiz.explain: 'If and only if' joins a statement with its converse when both are true.
quiz.mistake: Reads 'if and only if' as just 'if'

quiz.q: 'If n is odd, then n² is odd' is true. Is its converse 'If n² is odd, then n is odd' true?
options: Yes: if n were even, n² would be even, so n must be odd
No: 9 is odd but 3 is not
No: the converse of a true statement is always false
quiz.explain: If n were even, n² = n × n would be even. So whenever n² is odd, n must be odd. Both directions are true.
quiz.mistake: Thinks converses are always false, which is just as wrong as thinking they are always true

teach.ask: Gappu says: "'If it is a parrot, it is a bird' is true. So 'If it is a bird, it is a parrot' must also be true, right?"
teach.praise: The converse swaps the two parts, and it can be false. A crow is a bird but not a parrot! Thanks for saving me from a silly mistake.
teach.nudge: What happens when you swap the 'if' and 'then' parts? Can you think of a bird that is not a parrot?

learn.hook: Kabir checked 100 examples and says his rule always works. A mathematician smiles: 'Show me a proof that covers ALL numbers, even the ones you didn't try!'
points: A proof is a chain of logical steps that shows a statement is true in every case, starting from facts already accepted.
Axioms are basic facts accepted without proof. Theorems are statements that have been proved. A conjecture is believed true but not yet proved.
Checking examples can suggest a pattern, but it can never prove a statement about all numbers.
Use algebra to cover all cases: an even number is 2m and an odd number is 2m + 1, for some integer m.
To disprove a statement about all cases, one counterexample is enough.

example.q: Prove that the sum of two odd numbers is always even.
steps: Let the odd numbers be 2m + 1 and 2n + 1, where m and n are integers
This is 2 times an integer, so it is even, whatever m and n are
example.answer: The sum is 2(m + n + 1), which is always even.

learn.reallife: Online banking is safe because of number facts that mathematicians have proved. Engineers rely on proved results, not lucky guesses, to make bridges stand.

games.title: Prove: odd + odd = even
items: Let the numbers be 2m + 1 and 2n + 1
Add them: 2m + 2n + 2
Take out 2: 2(m + n + 1)
2 times an integer is even, so the sum is even

games.title: Words of proof
pairs: Axiom
A basic fact accepted without proof
Theorem
A statement that has been proved
Conjecture
Believed to be true but not yet proved
Counterexample
One case that shows a claim is false
Converse
Statement with hypothesis and conclusion swapped

quiz.q: Kabir checks 1 + 3 = 4, 3 + 5 = 8 and 5 + 7 = 12, and says: 'The sum of two odd numbers is always even. Proved!' What is wrong?
options: Nothing, three examples are a proof
Examples alone cannot prove a statement for all numbers
quiz.explain: The statement is true, but checking a few cases is not a proof. A proof must work for every pair of odd numbers, for example using 2m + 1 and 2n + 1.
quiz.mistake: Believes that enough examples make a proof

quiz.q: Which expression stands for any odd number, if m is an integer?
quiz.explain: 2m is always even, so one more than it, 2m + 1, is always odd.
quiz.mistake: Thinks m + 1 is always odd, but it is even when m is odd

quiz.q: The sum of three consecutive integers n, n + 1, n + 2 is 3n + 3. Which number always divides this sum?
quiz.explain: 3n + 3 = 3(n + 1), so the sum is always a multiple of 3. It is not always even: 2 + 3 + 4 = 9.
quiz.mistake: Generalises from 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 and says 6

quiz.q: What do we call a basic fact that is accepted without proof?
quiz.explain: Axioms are the starting points of reasoning; theorems are proved from them.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up theorems (proved) with axioms (assumed)

quiz.q: (2m + 1)(2n + 1) = 4mn + 2m + 2n + 1. What does this prove about the product of two odd numbers?
options: It is always a multiple of 4
quiz.explain: 4mn + 2m + 2n + 1 = 2(2mn + m + n) + 1, which is one more than an even number, so it is odd.
quiz.mistake: Sees the even terms 4mn, 2m and 2n and forgets the + 1

quiz.q: Goldbach's conjecture says every even number greater than 2 is the sum of two primes. What is its status?
options: It has been checked for very many numbers but not yet proved
It has been shown false by a counterexample
quiz.explain: Computers have checked it for enormous numbers, but nobody has found a proof yet, so it is still a conjecture.
quiz.mistake: Thinks checking very many cases turns a conjecture into a theorem

quiz.q: How many counterexamples are needed to show that a statement about all numbers is false?
quiz.explain: A claim about ALL cases fails as soon as one case breaks it.
quiz.mistake: Thinks you need many failures to disprove a general claim

quiz.q: In the usual proof that the angles of a triangle add up to 180°, a line is drawn through one vertex parallel to the opposite side. Which fact is used next?
options: Alternate angles made by a transversal with parallel lines are equal
The diagonals of a square are equal
quiz.explain: The two alternate angles equal two angles of the triangle, and together with the third angle they form a straight angle of 180°.
quiz.mistake: Tries to use a special triangle instead of facts that work for every triangle

teach.ask: Gappu tested 50 pairs of even numbers and their sum was always even: "Isn't that a proof?"
teach.praise: Examples are not enough: a proof must cover every case. Using 2m + 2n = 2(m + n) proves it for all even numbers at once!
teach.nudge: What about the numbers you didn't test? How can you show it works for every even number?
